original_value: This study proposes an adaptive compressed sensing (CS) method for video recovery based on spatial–temporal difference saliency in compressive domain. Firstly, the theoretical framework of realtime adaptive CS for video restoration is established, which includes two components: on‐chip and off‐chip. Secondly, the computation model of compressive domain spatial–temporal difference‐based saliency detection is built, which merely depends on the intra‐frame and inter‐frame similarities of compressive measurements. Thirdly, binary‐group approximation algorithm of subrate allocation is presented to achieve a quasi‐optimal solution. Finally, simulation experiments are designed to evaluate the performance of the proposed method, and it is indicated by the experimental results that the proposed method is suitable for realtime implementation and holds higher peak signal to noise ratio compared with the state‐of‐the‐art methods.

result.paraphrase: This study presents an adaptive compressed sensing (CS) approach for video recovery based on spatial–temporal difference saliency in the compressive domain. First, it establishes a theoretical framework for real-time adaptive CS in video restoration, comprising on-chip and off-chip components. Second, it develops a computation model for compressive-domain spatial–temporal difference saliency detection, relying only on intra-frame and inter-frame similarities of compressive measurements. Third, it introduces a binary-group approximation algorithm for subrate allocation to obtain a quasi-optimal solution. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to assess the proposed method, and the results show that it is suitable for real-time implementation and achieves a higher peak signal-to-noise ratio than state-of-the-art methods.
